full_judgment: 17. We have not allowed either of the parties to challenge the decisions and findings recorded by the other Division Bench with regard to issue Nos. 1 and 2 as we are not sitting over an appeal against their decision. The defendant, it appears, did not move the higher forum against the judgment and order passed by the other Division Bench on 19-5-1994 deciding issue Nos. 1 and 2 against the defendant. We have considered the decision cited by the learned Advocate Mrs Sufia Ahmed reported in 47 DLR (AD) 45 and also at 441. The proposition of law laid down in the decision is well settled but the facts and circumstance are quite distinguishable. In the present case PW 1 has explained the reason for non-examination of the captain of vessel stating that his whereabouts was not known to him. There is therefore, no scope for taking any adverse presumption for non-examination of the captain who was in charge of the vessel when it sank under section 61 of the Evidence Act. We do not therefore find that the decision referred to by the learned Advocate for the appellant has any application in the facts of the present case.
